The Redevelopment Authorities report also indicates the following:
"Through contact with various real estate agencies within the city of Harrisburg the LPA has determined that the estimated average vacancy rate for private rental units is approximately seventy units per year. The total number of private available sales units, based on a recent survey conducted by a number of realtors in the greater Harribsurg area, approximately three hundred units ranging in all bedroom sizes. In January of this year the U. S. Postal Department conducted a survey in Harrisburg to determine the total number of vacant dwellings in the City. As a result of this survey it has been found that approximately 2100 structures in Harrisburg are unoccupied and could ultimately provide housing resources."
The above figures indicate that an ample number of housing units will be available; however, less positive, it must be noted:
a. Due to the existence of other Federally financial programs in the city, also requiring relocation resources, there will be an increasing amount of competition for rental and purchase units. This demand could coincide with the demand generated by the project.
b. Virtually all of the units committed by the Housing Authority are occupied, and it appears that the agency will have to rely largely on turnover of the committed units for use by project relocatees.
